coordinate_semantics.correction: Darwin Core Point coordinates repeat meter mark 0 and are not literal meter-mark coordinates; vegetated meter-mark coordinates were reconstructed from the pinned transect start coordinate, signed bearing parsed from locationRemarks, and numeric meter-mark distance from child Point locationID.
coordinate_semantics.start_coordinate: pinned Darwin Core transect meter mark 0
coordinate_semantics.bearing: signed bearing parsed from pinned locationRemarks; generated from original TBEP transect LINESTRING
coordinate_semantics.meter_mark_distance: numeric suffix of child Point locationID

primary_thalassia_counterfactual_feasibi.interpretation: The nested counterfactual target is geographically feasible for the future Thalassia-positive cohort before field depth/forcing/wake qualification.

interpretation: After correcting point-coordinate semantics and reconstructing actual vegetated meter-mark positions along each fixed transect, the frozen GIS feasibility gate passes strongly. The earlier transect-start-only audit was a coordinate-resolution artifact and is superseded. GIS proximity is reconnaissance only; it does not certify a matched bare control.
decision: Retain the 18-node target and 12-node / 3-per-bay minimum for the nested canopy counterfactual. Proceed to preregistered field qualification without relaxing the 100-m threshold.
claim_boundary: A reconstructed vegetated meter mark within 100 m of mapped meadow edge is only a reconnaissance candidate, not a validated bare control.
Field validation must still satisfy depth matching, comparable forcing, substrate/context, wake screening and simultaneous sensor geometry.
Do not relax the frozen 100-m / 12-node / 3-per-bay thresholds after inspection.
The corrected result supersedes the earlier start-coordinate-only GIS audit.
No future biological response is used.
